decisions.label: Byte order
evidence: The binary header only makes sense read this way.

decisions.label: Samples per trace
evidence: File size divides exactly into traces of this length.

decisions.label: Sample format
evidence: IBM-normalisation test on 40,000 non-zero samples: 0.00% have a zero leading fraction digit (genuine IBM floats: 0%; IEEE floats: typically 5-10%).
This agrees with the declared format.

decisions.label: Data type
evidence: Bytes 189-192 and 193-196 together give a unique grid position for 100.0% of 1200 sampled traces; the first stays constant for runs of traces while the second steps by 1.
The inline number is also stored in byte(s) 191; byte 189 was chosen as the conventional location.
The crossline number is also stored in byte(s) 195; byte 193 was chosen as the conventional location.
Coordinates in bytes 181 and 185 are an exact linear function of (inline, crossline): residual 0.04% of a bin, a perfect regular grid.

evidence: Bytes 189-192 and 193-196 together give a unique grid position for 100.0% of 1200 sampled traces; the first stays constant for runs of traces while the second steps by 1.

Coordinates in bytes 181 and 185 are an exact linear function of (inline, crossline): residual 0.04% of a bin, a perfect regular grid.

decisions.label: Crossline number
evidence: Bytes 189-192 and 193-196 together give a unique grid position for 100.0% of 1200 sampled traces; the first stays constant for runs of traces while the second steps by 1.
The crossline number is also stored in byte(s) 195; byte 193 was chosen as the conventional location.

decisions.label: X coordinate (easting)
evidence: Coordinates in bytes 181 and 185 are an exact linear function of (inline, crossline): residual 0.04% of a bin, a perfect regular grid.
Across all traces, positions deviate from a perfect grid by 0.0407 units RMS; 0 traces are more than half a bin off.

decisions.label: Coordinate scalar
evidence: With scalar -10 the bin/trace spacing is 82.500 ft, a standard survey size.

evidence: Several CRSs fit equally well: EPSG:26715, EPSG:26716, EPSG:26717.

issues.title: Coordinate system needs choosing
issues.detail: Candidates: EPSG:26715 (NAD27 / UTM zone 15N), EPSG:26716 (NAD27 / UTM zone 16N), EPSG:26717 (NAD27 / UTM zone 17N), EPSG:26714 (NAD27 / UTM zone 14N). Several CRSs fit equally well: EPSG:26715, EPSG:26716, EPSG:26717.
issues.fix: Choose the CRS with --crs EPSG:xxxx (or in the web app). Ask the data supplier if unsure.
issues.explain: Several map projections fit the clues equally well, or the clues contradict the coordinates. Loading with the wrong one shifts the survey by metres to hundreds of kilometres.
